newsitem.title: GERMANY: German grain crops tolerating cool weather.
newsitem.headline: German grain crops tolerating cool weather.

text.p: German grain crops can tolerate relatively cool weather for the time of year without suffering damage, the national meteorological office DWD said on Friday.
A DWD source said rapeseed and sugar beet also escaped unscathed but warmer temperatures were needed in June for the more sensitive oilseed and beet.
Temperatures between nine and 18 degrees C over the last week were accompanied by light night frosts in some regions which hurt vegetables, DWD's weekly farm weather report said.
Moisture levels were generally sufficient but some deficits were noted in between the Main and Danube rivers in the south of Germany while the country's north received more rainfall.
Farmers were cutting grass for silage which would help reduce the demand for bought-in feeds in the summer.
Forecasts for the next seven days were for mostly dry weather with maximum day temperatures at 22 degrees.
